title: Unified Logistics Portal Integration
business: A regional logistics provider managing a fleet of delivery vehicles and warehouse inventory systems.
problem: The company suffers from fragmented service access where mobile drivers and warehouse staff must authenticate against five different backend microservices, leading to inconsistent security policies and high latency due to multiple round-trip handshakes.
solution: Implementing an API Gateway provides one managed entry point that routes and governs calls to backend services, centralizing authentication, rate limiting, and request transformation before traffic reaches internal systems.
steps: Define a single public-facing endpoint that maps to internal service routes.
Configure the gateway to handle centralized authentication and authorization tokens.
Implement request routing logic to direct traffic to specific backend services based on URL paths.
Apply cross-cutting concerns like logging and rate limiting at the gateway level.
Expose a unified interface to clients, hiding the complexity of the underlying microservice architecture.
outcome: Clients interact with a single, secure entry point, reducing client-side complexity and ensuring uniform security enforcement across all backend services.
limitation: The gateway can become a single point of failure or a performance bottleneck; check this by monitoring the latency and error rates of the gateway service specifically under peak load.
